THE EXPERIMENT

Small brain.
Ambitious career change.

The network includes 166,700 annotated neurons, 25,582,938 directed connections, and 124,177,617 synaptic contacts from MaleCNS v1.0. Every connection between retained, annotated non-glial neurons is included, with no weight cutoff.

The brain’s shape comes from 3,487,943 measured synaptic endpoints and soma fallbacks. Drawing samples one in 128 endpoints plus a measured anchor per located neuron; graph computation keeps all retained edges. This is a point cloud of measured anatomy, not complete neuron skeletons. 121 neurons have no available position and participate in the network without a drawn location. Brain view crops the nerve cord; Whole CNS reveals it.

A brain in the loop

All retained connections propagate a simplified signed rate signal in a background worker. Flight telemetry drives annotated sensory groups through an engineered interface. The full network feeds back into a 96-neuron motor circuit with 18 engineered sensor channels and 10 control outputs. The outputs move throttle, two-axis gimbal, attitude jets, fins, engine selector and head orientation. Bounded control travel introduces an actuator delay; inverse kinematics positions the fly’s limbs on the controls. Individual limb joints are not learned from scratch. The displayed Hz is the actual network update rate, independent of flight playback speed.

What actually learns?

Reward-based evolution strategies adjust 190 motor-output coefficients and 12 gain groups on existing motor-circuit connections. The 3D model transfers the earlier landing policy to both lateral axes, then trains the expanded outputs on new descents. Fast candidate flights use the latest frozen full-network feedback; the whole graph runs continuously during live flight. Training runs on your device and saves a local checkpoint.

The dynamics, sensory interface, synaptic signs and learning rule are modeling choices. Activity is computed, not recorded biological firing. This is an experimental connectome-driven controller, not a validated emulation of a living fly. There is no language model flying the rocket. Head turns sample numerical fuel and engine-health readings; other flight cues remain available. This is instrument-assisted control, not learned raw-pixel vision. Expressions and radio jokes are cosmetic reactions to flight state.

The fictional vehicle

This stylized 3D booster has a center engine and a selectable three-engine bank, four grid fins, attitude jets, and a tiny Dragon-style crew pod with an antenna. Thrust, aerodynamics, faults and landing tolerances are game-scale approximations. It is not a flight-qualified Falcon 9 model. Eight missions progress from calm descents to combined faults. The final mission completely shuts off the center engine. Night lighting and fog affect the spectator view; the pilot retains engineered flight cues.

Try an experiment

Click a neuron to inspect its source ID and annotation, then pulse it to inject eight network updates of excitation. Spotlight the motor circuit to see where commands leave the brain. Throw a gust to challenge recovery, or take the controls yourself.

The starter checkpoints were evaluated with the original motor circuit. Those results are not a validation of this expanded network.

The complete anatomy and graph download about 91 MB on first use. The motor pilot starts while they load. A current desktop browser with WebGL 2 works best.
